title: Proper compact-support and tensor comparisons identify etale and pro-etale projection maps
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $C_W=\nu_W^*$ for the derived comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Let $D^b_{ctf}$ mean bounded constructible complexes whose derived tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

For the identity-open compactification put $F_e=Ri_{e,*}$, $F_p=Ri_{p,*}$, $G_e=i^\times$ and $G_p=C_ZG_eR\nu_{T,*}$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Let $b_B:C_TF_eB\xrightarrow{\sim}F_pC_ZB$ be the canonical direct-image mate of the ordinary pullback comparison, normalized to commute with the ordinary pullback/direct-image counits. Put $\eta_B=b_B^{-1}$. Use the exceptional adjunction on bounded-below etale-origin objects transported by the site-comparison unit, and write $\mu^e,\mu^p$ for its counits. Here the transported Hom bijection is specified as follows: for $H\in D^+(Z_e,A)$ and $L\in D^+(T_p,A)$ it is the composite
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F_pC_ZH,L)\xrightarrow{(-)\circ b_H}\operatorname{Hom}(C_TF_eH,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_eH,R\nu_{T,*}L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,G_eR\nu_{T,*}L)\xrightarrow{C_Z}\operatorname{Hom}(C_ZH,G_pL),$$
using the ordinary etale exceptional adjunction [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], the comparison adjunction and its full faithfulness [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Thus the transported counit is the inverse image of the identity under this specified Hom bijection, at an etale-origin representative of $G_pL$. Then for bounded constructible $N$ with $G_eN$ bounded constructible, under $G_pC_TN\cong C_ZG_eN$,
$$\mu^p_{C_TN}=C_T(\mu^e_N)\circ\eta_{G_eN}.$$
For $B\in D^b_c(Z_e,A)$ and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(T_e,A)$ let $\pi_e:F_eB\otimes_A^LM\to F_e(B\otimes_A^Li_e^*M)$ and $\pi_p:F_pC_ZB\otimes_A^LC_TM\to F_p(C_ZB\otimes_A^Li_p^*C_TM)$ be the canonical ordinary-counit-defined projection transformations, on the etale site as in [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and on either ringed topos as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Explicitly, for $\tau=e,p$, let $l_\tau=i_\tau^*$, $r_\tau=Ri_{\tau,*}$, and let $u^\tau,\varepsilon^\tau$ be the unit and counit of $l_\tau\dashv r_\tau$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $t_{l_\tau}:l_\tau(X\otimes^LY)\xrightarrow{\sim}l_\tau X\otimes^Ll_\tau Y$ be the canonical derived tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. On both sites the definition is
$$\pi^\tau_{E,K}=r_\tau\bigl((\varepsilon^\tau_E\otimes1)\circ t_{l_\tau;r_\tau E,K}\bigr)\circ u^\tau_{r_\tau E\otimes^LK}.$$
Here $(E,K)=(B,M)$ for $e$ and $(E,K)=(C_ZB,C_TM)$ for $p$. Under the monoidal comparison and $i_p^*C_T\cong C_Zi_e^*$, their precise compatibility is
$$\eta_{B\otimes_A^Li_e^*M}\circ\pi_p=C_T(\pi_e)\circ(\eta_B\otimes1_{C_TM}).$$
This equality is an equality of the named transformations, including their inverses whenever the finite-stage projection formula makes them invertible.

source.place: Second proof paragraph: both maps correspond to the restriction of evaluation; ordinary-to-pro-etale realization, counit and projection normalization in returned step 9.

proof.text:
A closed immersion is proper, so the compactification is $(1_Z,i)$. Its two compact-support functors are $F_e=Ri_{e,*}$ and $F_p=Ri_{p,*}$: extension by zero along $1_Z$ is the identity. A field is Noetherian, and finite type over it makes $Z,T$ Noetherian. The ordinary etale exceptional-adjoint theorem therefore gives $F_e\dashv G_e$. The affine description of a closed immersion is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$; in particular $i$ is affine and quasi-compact and separated, so the canonical-direct-image-mate theorem applies. It gives the specified natural isomorphism $b:C_TF_e\to F_pC_Z$. With $l=i_e^*$, $P=i_p^*$ and $a:C_Zl\to PC_T$, its normalization is
$$\varepsilon^p_{C_ZH}\circ P(b_H)=C_Z(\varepsilon^e_H)\circ a_{F_eH}^{-1}.$$
Set $\eta=b^{-1}$. No identification of an unspecified isomorphism with $b$ is used.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint) and 07A7 (remark-base-change); canonical counit normalization as in categories.tex Tag 0B65. The ordinary exceptional adjoint is supplied by the cited existing theorem, not by these tags.

proof.text:
The finite formula for the exceptional inverse image is $G_p=C_ZG_eR
u_{T,*}$, with its bounded-below typing already supplied by the cited definition. For bounded-below $H,L$ the transported Hom bijection is the one written in the statement: first precompose with $b_H$, then apply $C_T\dashv R
u_{T,*}$, then $F_e\dashv G_e$, then the fully faithful functor $C_Z$. Each arrow is a bijection, and they are natural. The unit $j_N:N	o R
u_{T,*}C_TN$ is invertible; thus $C_ZG_e(j_N)$ identifies $C_ZG_eN$ with $G_pC_TN$. For $L=C_TN$, this specializes, under that identification, to
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F_pC_ZH,C_TN)\xrightarrow{(-)\circ b_H}\operatorname{Hom}(C_TF_eH,C_TN)\xrightarrow{C_T^{-1}}\operatorname{Hom}(F_eH,N)\xrightarrow{F_e\dashv G_e}\operatorname{Hom}(H,G_eN)\xrightarrow{C_Z}\operatorname{Hom}(C_ZH,C_ZG_eN).$$
Here $C_T^{-1}$ means the inverse map on Hom sets furnished by full faithfulness, not an inverse functor on the ambient pro-etale category.

source.place: Tag 0DV0 (lemma-compose-counits), explicitly composing the displayed Hom bijections; specialization to fully faithful comparison pullbacks.

proof.text:
Put $H=G_eN$, which is bounded below by the hypothesis that $G_eN$ is bounded constructible. Apply the specialized Hom chain of Step 2 to $C_T(\mu^e_N)\circ b_H^{-1}$. Precomposing with $b_H$ gives $C_T(\mu^e_N)$; the inverse of $C_T$ on Hom sets gives $\mu^e_N$; ordinary exceptional adjunction sends its counit to $1_{G_eN}$; applying $C_Z$ gives $1_{C_ZG_eN}$. The transported counit is precisely the preimage of that identity. Bijectivity proves
$$\mu^p_{C_TN}=C_T(\mu^e_N)\circ\eta_{G_eN}$$
under $C_ZG_e(j_N)$. This computes the counit of the specified transported adjunction, rather than asserting the existence of an ambient pro-etale exceptional adjoint.

source.place: Tag 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints); evaluation at the identity in the Hom transport of Step 2.

proof.text:
Use $l,P,a$ from Step 1. For each derived pullback $J$, write $t_J:J(U\otimes^LV)\to JU\otimes^LJV$ for its tensor comparison. The etale/pro-etale pullback comparison $a:C_Zl\to PC_T$ comes from the commuting comparison square of topoi. The comparison morphisms are flat ringed-topos morphisms with the identified constant ring sheaves. All four inverse images carry each scalar endomorphism for a fixed element of $A$ to that same scalar endomorphism; the structure maps preserve constant sections. Hence the structural ring maps commute with the comparison square, as can be checked on the constant-section generators before sheafification. The ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons theorem, applied to the two composites around this square and its specified 2-isomorphism, shows that $a$ is monoidal for these actual tensor comparisons. In components the equation needed below is
$$t_P\circ P(t_{C_T})\circ a_{U\otimes^LV}=(a_U\otimes a_V)\circ t_{C_Z}\circ C_Z(t_l).$$
This equation has source $C_Zl(U\otimes^LV)$ and target $PC_TU\otimes^LPC_TV$.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), and the comparisons in Tag 0E48 (remark-compatible-with-diagram).

proof.text:
Put $Q=B\otimes_A^LlM$, and let
$$h=(1\otimes a_M)\circ t_{C_Z;B,lM}:C_ZQ\xrightarrow{\sim}C_ZB\otimes_A^LPC_TM.$$
The finite-Tor condition on $M$ gives a bounded flat etale model by the etale clause of the flat-model theorem. A bounded flat complex is K-flat: filter it by its finitely many terms, tensor with any acyclic complex, and use exactness of tensor by a flat sheaf and the cohomology sequence at each finite filtration step. The ringed-topos pullback theorem says that pullback carries K-flat complexes with flat terms to such complexes. As $l$ is exact at constant coefficients, pulling this model back gives a bounded flat model of $lM$. If $B$ has cohomology in $[r,s]$ and that model is supported in $[u,v]$, tensoring it with a good bounded representative of $B$ has terms only in $[r+u,s+v]$. Hence $Q$ is bounded, in particular in $D^+$, so $b_Q$ is defined and invertible. Use on both sites the ringed-topos projection transformation: its transpose is exactly $(\varepsilon^\tau_E\otimes1)t_{l_\tau}$. For the etale site this agrees term for term with the explicit definition in def-kun-projection-formula-map; the pro-etale definition is supplied by the general ringed-topos theorem and the derived adjunction of the pro-etale operations.

source.place: Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map), using Tags 07A4 and 07A6; bounded flat models are taken from the cited flat-model statement.

proof.text:
Let $X=C_TF_eB\otimes_A^LC_TM$ and $Y=C_ZB\otimes_A^LPC_TM$. Both maps to compare are now written with the same source and target $X\to F_pY$:
$$L=F_p(h)\circ b_Q\circ C_T(\pi_e)\circ t_{C_T;F_eB,M}^{-1},\qquad R=\pi_p\circ(b_B\otimes1).$$
Under $P\dashv F_p$, transposition sends $f:X\to F_pY$ to $\varepsilon^p_Y\circ P(f)$. Naturality of the counit and the normalization of $b_Q$ give
$$L^\flat=h\circ C_Z(\varepsilon^e_Q)\circ a_{F_eQ}^{-1}\circ PC_T(\pi_e)\circ P(t_{C_T}^{-1}).$$
Naturality of $a$ moves $PC_T(\pi_e)$ through $a^{-1}$. The defining transpose identity $\varepsilon^e_Q\circ l(\pi_e)=(\varepsilon^e_B\otimes1)t_l$ then yields
$$L^\flat=h\circ C_Z((\varepsilon^e_B\otimes1)t_l)\circ a_{F_eB\otimes^LM}^{-1}\circ P(t_{C_T}^{-1}).$$

source.place: Tag 0E48 (remark-compatible-with-diagram): verification of the left route by the counit formula for an adjunct, rather than its omitted verification.

proof.text:
For the other route, the pro-etale projection definition and naturality of $t_P$ give
$$R^\flat=(\varepsilon^p_{C_ZB}\otimes1)\circ t_P\circ P(b_B\otimes1)=((\varepsilon^p_{C_ZB}\circ P(b_B))\otimes1)\circ t_{P;C_TF_eB,C_TM}.$$
Insert the normalization of $b_B$ from Step 1. Apply the monoidality equation of Step 4 with $U=F_eB,V=M$, solving for $t_P$ by the inverses of $P(t_{C_T})$ and $a$. This gives
$$R^\flat=(C_Z(\varepsilon^e_B)\otimes a_M)\circ t_{C_Z;lF_eB,lM}\circ C_Z(t_{l;F_eB,M})\circ a_{F_eB\otimes^LM}^{-1}\circ P(t_{C_T}^{-1}).$$
Naturality of $t_{C_Z}$ moves $C_Z(\varepsilon^e_B\otimes1)$ across it; the first factors become $h\circ C_Z((\varepsilon^e_B\otimes1)t_l)$. Thus $R^\flat=L^\flat$, with exactly the common composite displayed in Step 6.

source.place: Tag 0E48 (remark-compatible-with-diagram): verification of the right route, using the canonical tensor and counit comparisons.

proof.text:
Transposition under $P\dashv F_p$ is injective, so Steps 6 and 7 give $L=R$. Substitute their expressions and compose with the inverses of $F_p(h)$ and $b_Q$. After the specified tensor identifications, $b_Q^{-1}=\eta_Q$ and $b_B^{-1}=\eta_B$, and the result is precisely
$$\eta_{B\otimes_A^LlM}\circ\pi_p=C_T(\pi_e)\circ(\eta_B\otimes1).$$
If the finite-stage projection formula makes $\pi_e$ invertible, this equality and the isomorphisms $b,t_{C_T},h$ make $\pi_p$ invertible as well. Inverting the displayed equality gives
$$\pi_p^{-1}\circ\eta_Q^{-1}=(\eta_B^{-1}\otimes1)\circ C_T(\pi_e^{-1}),$$
under the same identifications. This proves the claimed compatibility of inverses whenever they exist, without invoking a separate pro-etale projection theorem.

source.place: Tag 0E48 (remark-compatible-with-diagram), concluding by injectivity of the adjunction bijection and elementary inversion of isomorphisms.
